blogs.title: The Consistency Trap: Why the TTAB Must Align Its DuPont Scope
blogs.description: An analysis of the Federal Circuit's new doctrinal requirement for consistency across the DuPont factors. This post dissects the Hughes opinion's criticism of the Board for narrowing the definition of 'similar services' when applying the sixth factor after broadly defining them for the second factor, establishing a new procedural constraint for trademark likelihood of confusion hearings.

blogs.title: Banking or Credit Cards? How Dictionary Definitions Expand Trademark Protection
blogs.description: A detailed look at the semantic battleground of the second DuPont factor. This post explores the court's reliance on dictionary definitions to classify 'banking,' 'bank,' and 'finance' as legally identical to 'credit card services,' and how this expansive classification limits new entrants' ability to carve out distinct market niches under the Lanham Act.

blogs.title: Eroding Distinctiveness in a Crowded Field: The Standard for Commercial Strength
blogs.description: An examination of the third-party mark doctrine (DuPont Factor VI) and the Federal Circuit's vacatur of the Board's narrow 'credit card' scope. This post discusses the implications for establishing commercial strength, arguing that excluding broader third-party usage in related banking services undermines the legal threshold needed to prove a mark's inherent distinctiveness.
